non_blocking_findings: Guard hole: the vector-read pattern only matches ["vector"], .get("vector") with a closing paren, and .vector. Verified by injecting into the tree and running the recipe block: physics/blackbody.gd with d.get("vector", 0) exits 0 (not caught) and sky/background.gd with d.has("vector") exits 0. The positive control only proves the pattern matches its own four forms. .get(key, default) is the dominant idiom in this repo (the bridge itself uses .get("proto", {})), so the AC11 'no shipped .gd reads vector' claim is weaker than stated. The plan fixed this exact pattern, so it is a plan gap rather than an executor deviation.

SIMILAR_MINOR's value is not pinned. Setting it to 15 (mutation G) leaves every test green: the real-sim loop iterates [SIMILAR_MINOR, ARCHIVE_MINOR, EARTH_MINOR] and checks only that the negotiated minor equals the request, so the 2.14 case and the 2.14 tick test silently become a second 2.15 run, and the fake's hello still advertises 14. Suggest assert_bool(SimBridge.SIMILAR_MINOR == 14) or literal 14.

Amendment rule 4 says the bad_response condition is the typeof check and an empty {} is valid. No test sends an empty Dictionary, so a _take_similar that rejects {} (mutation Q) survives. The sim never sends {} at 14+, so risk is low.

_take_similar's store path is not tested for aliasing. Replacing parse_similar(changes["similar"]) with a bare changes["similar"] (mutation H) survives: deep copy is asserted only on parse_similar called directly. In production this would make bridge.similar alias state["changes"]["similar"].

Harness limitation (seen in mutation N): a GDScript runtime error inside a test body (SCRIPT ERROR in parse_similar for a non-Dictionary return) does not fail the run, because Godot returns a default value and the 'ran to completion' check still sees true. It was a type-invalid mutation, but it shows the runner exit code can be 0 while the log contains SCRIPT ERROR.

The Makefile pathspec '*.gd' (git pathspec * crosses /) already covers tests/ and every subdirectory, so the six other pathspecs are redundant. Dropping '*.gd' is EQUIVALENT today. An injected d["vector"] in tests/test_sim_bridge.gd fails the guard, contrary to the amendment's 'tests/ never named'. Harmless and stricter now, but a future test that mentions the key in a fixture would trip it.
The sprint JSON still has S0.3 status 'pending' (no completed timestamp, notes or passes). This is controller bookkeeping at landing. The sprint status is in_progress.

Plan T2 is folded into test_similar_real, which the amendment allows. The unknown-key and deep-copy checks run on a literal, not on a real-sim section. The 2.13 below-minor case uses SURFACE_MINOR (13) on the real sim as specified.

Not run (by instruction): make test. The rig/full status is separate. Local full-suite regression of other SimBridge callers is therefore covered only by test_sim_bridge.gd (107 ok, 98 base + 9 new, 0 failures).

rules_1_5.evidence: Rule 1 const SIMILAR_MINOR := 14 sits between SURFACE and ARCHIVE with a ## comment. Rule 2 var similar: Dictionary = {} with a ## comment, reset in new_game before the take chain. Rule 3 parse_similar is static, returns v.duplicate(true) for a Dictionary and {} otherwise, with no whitelist, rounding or recomputation (the GDScript never touches d or any field). Rule 4 _take_similar is absent -> true, non-Dictionary -> false (bad_response), Dictionary -> stored. Rule 5 _finish untouched. git diff --exit-code 530cdece -- main.gd sim/ gives rc 0. Diff sizes: bridge 21+2 (cap 30), tests 70 (cap 70), Makefile 11 (cap 20).
